recommended_next_step: Send or repeat a clean controller-side GDPR rights request before widening the route.
note: Use this when the complainant still lacks a clean documented first request.

recommended_next_step: Prepare and file the DPA complaint using the correct national intake route and preserve the chronology.
note: Use this when controller-side contact happened but the case is not yet with the regulator.

recommended_next_step: Keep the chronology clean and wait for acknowledgement or a procedural step before moving into pressure mode.
note: Do not escalate publicly too early if the complaint was only just filed.

recommended_next_step: Ask a specialist privacy NGO or watchdog to review or amplify the systemic pattern.
note: Best when one complainant has enough evidence to suggest a wider abusive pattern.

recommended_next_step: Turn the one-off chronology into a complaint package with repeat-pattern evidence and regulator-ready framing.
note: Useful before or alongside a formal complaint when the issue is bigger than one person.

recommended_next_step: Coordinate complainants and align the timeline, lead-authority clues, and factual framing before wider escalation.
note: Use this before approaching multiple outside actors with inconsistent facts.

recommended_next_step: Use the controller-establishment and OSS reference layers to make a first evidence-backed lead-DPA assessment.
note: This is a strategy step rather than an outward-facing escalation.

recommended_next_step: Bring in a privacy watchdog or coalition route once the cross-border framing is documented.
note: Best when several complainants or jurisdictions are involved and the complaint has public-interest value.

recommended_next_step: Send a procedural follow-up to the DPA before moving into external pressure.
note: This should normally happen before journalist or parliamentary outreach.

recommended_next_step: Ask a privacy NGO or watchdog to assess the enforcement-failure pattern and help validate escalation.
note: Use once the silence or under-action is documented clearly enough to explain to an outside actor.

recommended_next_step: Pitch the enforcement-delay story to a journalist only after the chronology and public-interest angle are clean.
note: Do not use for thinly evidenced personal disputes.

recommended_next_step: Raise the under-enforcement pattern with an MEP when oversight pressure is more suitable than media-first escalation.
note: Useful where Commission, EDPB, or cross-border oversight angles matter.
